You said:
what is a no code platform? How would I set that up so that people can visit a URL for now
ChatGPT said:
ChatGPT said:

A no-code platform lets you build and deploy web apps without writing code. It’s ideal if you want to create something functional quickly without learning programming. Popular options include:

  1. Bubble.io – Drag-and-drop builder, flexible but has a learning curve.
  2. Glide – Great for simple apps, uses Google Sheets as a database.
  3. Softr – Builds web apps on top of Airtable, user-friendly.
  4. Thunkable – Good for turning a web app into a mobile app.

How to Set It Up for a Public URL:

Option 1: Bubble.io (Recommended)

  1. Sign up on Bubble.io.
  2. Create a new app.
  3. Use their drag-and-drop editor to design a simple interface with:
    • Buttons for rolling dice and drawing cards.
    • A text box to display results.
  4. Use their "Workflows" feature to add logic:
    • A workflow for dice rolling (Random: 1 to 20).
    • A workflow for drawing a card (Pick random item from list).
  5. Deploy the app (Bubble will give you a free subdomain, e.g., yourapp.bubbleapps.io).

Option 2: Hosting Your React Code on Vercel

Since you already have a React component, you can:

  1. Create a free account on Vercel.
  2. Install Node.js and Git if you don’t have them.
  3. Clone a simple Next.js project and replace it with your code.
  4. Deploy with a single command: vercel.
  5. Vercel will generate a free URL like pale-tides.vercel.app.

Would you like me to guide you through Bubble.io setup or Vercel deployment in more detail?

To deploy your PALE TIDES Dice Roller online for testing, follow these steps:

Option 1: Deploy with Vercel (Recommended for React)

Vercel is great for React-based projects and provides a free hosting option.

1. Install Node.js and Git

You'll need Node.js and Git installed on your computer.

  • Download Node.js
  • Download Git

2. Install Vercel CLI

Run this in your terminal:

sh
npm install -g vercel

3. Create a React Project (if you haven't)

If your project isn't inside a React app yet, create one:

sh
npx create-next-app@latest pale-tides-dice-roller
cd pale-tides-dice-roller

Then, replace the default index.js or index.tsx file with your Dice Roller code.

4. Deploy to Vercel

Inside your project folder, run:

sh
vercel

It will prompt you to log in (sign up if needed) and ask a few deployment questions. Use the default settings.

5. Get Your Live URL

After deploying, Vercel will give you a URL like:

arduino
https://pale-tides-dice-roller.vercel.app

This is your public test link!

Option 2: Deploy with Netlify (Another Easy Option)

  1. Install Netlify CLI:

    sh
    npm install -g netlify-cli

  2. Deploy the Project:

    sh
    netlify deploy --prod

    Follow the steps, and Netlify will provide a public URL.

Option 3: Use GitHub Pages (Basic Hosting)

If you want a static React app, you can deploy it via GitHub Pages.

  1. Push your project to GitHub.
  2. Install GitHub Pages dependency:
    sh
    npm install gh-pages --save-dev
  3. Add this to your package.json:
    json
    "scripts": {
  "predeploy": "npm run build",
  "deploy": "gh-pages -d build"
}
  4. Deploy with:
    sh
    npm run deploy
  5. Your Dice Roller will be live at:
    arduino
    https://your-username.github.io/pale-tides-dice-roller/

Which Option Should You Choose?

  • Use Vercel if you want a quick, free, and easy way to host a React app.
  • Use Netlify if you're familiar with it or prefer drag-and-drop deployment.
  • Use GitHub Pages if you want a static version and prefer GitHub integration.

Let me know which option sounds best, and I can guide you through any steps! 🚀

ok I tested this but on mobile I can't edit the numbers (the default of 1 can't be changed beyond adding additional numbers to it)
ChatGPT said:

The issue with number inputs on mobile happens because mobile browsers often append numbers instead of replacing them. Let's fix it:

Fix: Ensure Full Editing of Number Inputs

Modify the onChange handlers for the number inputs so that they properly update when typing on mobile.

Changes:

  • Prevent unwanted NaN values.
  • Ensure numbers can be fully edited instead of always appending.

Updated Code for Inputs

Modify the onChange handlers like this:

jsx
<input 
  type="number" 
  value={numDice} 
  onChange={(e) => {
    let value = e.target.value;
    if (value === "") {
      setNumDice(""); // Allow clearing the input
    } else {
      setNumDice(Math.max(1, parseInt(value) || 1));
    }
  }} 
  className="border p-2 rounded w-16 text-center"
/>

<input 
  type="number" 
  value={difficulty} 
  onChange={(e) => {
    let value = e.target.value;
    if (value === "") {
      setDifficulty(""); // Allow clearing the input
    } else {
      setDifficulty(Math.max(1, parseInt(value) || 1));
    }
  }} 
  className="border p-2 rounded w-16 text-center"
/>

Why This Fix Works

  1. Allows clearing the input (setNumDice("") lets the user delete numbers).
  2. Ensures valid numbers (converts input to a number properly).
  3. Prevents appending issues when typing on mobile keyboards.

Apply the Fix

  • Replace only the <input> elements inside src/App.js with the updated version above.
  • Save the file and restart the app:
    sh
    npm start

Now, on mobile, the inputs should behave correctly, letting users edit numbers freely. 🚀 Let me know if you need further tweaks!

jsx
import { useState } from "react";
import "./index.css"; // Import Tailwind styles

export default function DiceCardApp() {
  const [rollResults, setRollResults] = useState([]);
  const [numDice, setNumDice] = useState(1);
  const [difficulty, setDifficulty] = useState(1);
  const [notification, setNotification] = useState("");
  const [successMessage, setSuccessMessage] = useState("");
  const [successCount, setSuccessCount] = useState(0);
  const [failureCount, setFailureCount] = useState(0);

  const rollDice = (num) => {
    let initialRolls = [];
    let extraRolls = [];
    let finalDiceResults = [];
    let detailedResults = [];
    let exploded = false;

    // Roll initial dice
    for (let i = 0; i < num; i++) {
      let roll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1;
      initialRolls.push(roll);
      finalDiceResults.push(roll);
    }

    // Display initial rolls
    detailedResults.push(
      <p className="font-bold text-lg">
        You rolled: <span className="font-normal text-base">{initialRolls.join(", ")}</span>
      </p>
    );

    // Handle exploding sixes
    let explosionCount = initialRolls.filter((die) => die === 6).length;
    if (explosionCount > 0) {
      exploded = true;
      detailedResults.push(
        <p className="italic text-sm text-gray-600">Rolls of 6 explode! Rolling {explosionCount} extra dice:</p>
      );
      for (let i = 0; i < explosionCount; i++) {
        let extraRoll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1;
        extraRolls.push(extraRoll);
        finalDiceResults.push(extraRoll);
      }
      detailedResults.push(
        <p className="font-bold text-lg">
          You rolled: <span className="font-normal text-base">{extraRolls.join(", ")}</span>
        </p>
      );
    }

    // Sort final results high to low
    finalDiceResults.sort((a, b) => b - a);

    if (exploded) {
      detailedResults.push(
        <p className="font-bold text-lg">
          Final Dice Pool: <span className="font-bold">{finalDiceResults.join(", ")}</span>
        </p>
      );
    }

    detailedResults.push(
      <p className="italic text-sm text-gray-600">Successes: {successCount}, Failures: {failureCount}</p>
    );

    setRollResults(detailedResults);

    const countOnes = finalDiceResults.filter((die) => die === 1).length;
    const countSixes = finalDiceResults.filter((die) => die === 6).length;
    const newSuccessCount = finalDiceResults.filter((die) => die >= 4).length;
    const newFailureCount = finalDiceResults.length - newSuccessCount;

    setSuccessCount(newSuccessCount);
    setFailureCount(newFailureCount);

    if (countOnes >= 3 && countSixes >= 3) {
      setNotification("Boons and Banes cancelled each other out! The action is a success.");
    } else if (countOnes >= 3) {
      setNotification("Action triggered a BANE!");
    } else if (countSixes >= 3) {
      setNotification("Action triggered a BOON!");
    } else {
      setNotification("");
    }

    setSuccessMessage(newSuccessCount >= difficulty ? "ACTION SUCCEEDED!" : "ACTION FAILED!");
  };

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center p-6 space-y-6 bg-gray-100 min-h-screen text-center">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold text-blue-700">PALE TIDES Dice Roller</h1>
      <p className="italic text-gray-600">Experimental dice roller for internal testing</p>

      <div className="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg shadow-lg w-full max-w-xs space-y-2">
        <p className="text-lg font-bold">DICE RULES</p>
        <p className="italic text-sm text-gray-700">
          • Rolls of 4+ are successful. Match or beat the Task Difficulty to succeed at the task!<br />
          • 6's explode! Another dice is rolled.<br />
          • Rolling 3×6 results in a Boon!<br />
          • Rolling 3×1 results in a Bane!<br />
          • If you get a Boon and Bane, they cancel each other out.
        </p>
      </div>

      {/* Input fields */}
      <div className="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg shadow-lg w-full max-w-xs space-y-4">
        <label className="text-lg font-semibold">Dice</label>
        <input
          type="number"
          value={numDice}
          onChange={(e) => setNumDice(Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1))}
          className="border p-2 rounded w-full text-center"
        />
        <label className="text-lg font-semibold">Task Difficulty</label>
        <input
          type="number"
          value={difficulty}
          onChange={(e) => setDifficulty(Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1))}
          className="border p-2 rounded w-full text-center"
        />
        <button
          onClick={() => rollDice(numDice)}
          className="bg-blue-600 text-white px-6 py-2 rounded hover:bg-blue-800 w-full font-semibold text-lg"
        >
          Roll Dice
        </button>
      </div>

      {rollResults.length > 0 && (
        <div className="text-xl space-y-2 bg-white p-4 rounded-lg shadow-md w-full max-w-xs">
          {rollResults.map((res, index) => (
            <p key={index}>{res}</p>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}

      {successMessage && (
        <div className="bg-white p-4 rounded-lg shadow-lg w-full max-w-xs text-lg font-bold">
          <p className="text-blue-600">{successMessage}</p>
          {notification && <p className="text-black font-normal text-lg">{notification}</p>}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

ChatGPT said:

Embedding the Dice Roller in Squarespace

Squarespace doesn't allow JavaScript inside regular content blocks, so you'll need to embed the script correctly. Here's how to make it work:

✅ Step 1: Use a Code Block

  1. Log in to Squarespace and open the page where you want to add the dice roller.
  2. Click Edit Page → Add a Code Block.
  3. Paste this modified version of your code:
    html
    <div class="container">
    <h2>Pale Tides Dice Roller</h2>
    <p class="italic">Experimental dice roller for internal testing</p>
    <div class="result" style="margin-bottom: 15px;"> 
        <h3>Dice Rules</h3>
        <p class='italic' style='font-size: 14px;'>
            • Match or beat the Task Difficulty to succeed at the task!<br>
            • By default, rolls of <strong>4+</strong> are successful.<br>
            • If you have advantage, rolls of <strong>3+</strong> are successful.<br>
            • If you have disadvantage, rolls of <strong>5+</strong> are successful.<br>
            • <strong>6's explode!</strong> Another dice is rolled automatically.<br><br>
            • Rolling <strong>3×6</strong> results in a <strong>Boon</strong>!<br>
            • Rolling <strong>3×1</strong> results in a <strong>Bane</strong>!<br>
            • If you get a Boon and Bane, they cancel each other out.
        </p>
    </div>
    <div class="input-container">
        <label>Dice:</label>
        <input type="number" id="numDice" min="1" value="1">
    </div>
    <br>
    <div class="input-container">
        <label>Task Difficulty:</label>
        <input type="number" id="difficulty" min="1" value="1">
    </div>
    <br>
    <div class="input-container">
        <label>Advantage:</label>
        <input type="checkbox" id="advantage" onclick="toggleAdvantage()">
        <label>Disadvantage:</label>
        <input type="checkbox" id="disadvantage" onclick="toggleAdvantage()">
    </div>
    <br>
    <button class="button" onclick="rollDice()">Roll Dice</button>
    <div class="result" id="output" style="display: none;"></div>
</div>
  4. Click "Apply" to save.

✅ Step 2: Add JavaScript to Squarespace

  1. Go to Settings → Advanced → Code Injection.
  2. Under "Footer", paste the following JavaScript:
    html
    <script>
    function toggleAdvantage() {
        let advantage = document.getElementById('advantage');
        let disadvantage = document.getElementById('disadvantage');
        if (advantage.checked) {
            disadvantage.checked = false;
        } else if (disadvantage.checked) {
            advantage.checked = false;
        }
    }
    function rollDice() {
        let advantage = document.getElementById('advantage').checked;
        let disadvantage = document.getElementById('disadvantage').checked;
        let successThreshold = 4;
        if (advantage) successThreshold = 3;
        if (disadvantage) successThreshold = 5;
        let numDice = parseInt(document.getElementById('numDice').value) || 1;
        let difficulty = parseInt(document.getElementById('difficulty').value) || 1;
        let initialRolls = [];
        let extraRolls = [];
        let finalDiceResults = [];
        let output = document.getElementById('output');
        output.innerHTML = "";

        for (let i = 0; i < numDice; i++) {
            let roll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1;
            initialRolls.push(roll);
            finalDiceResults.push(roll);
        }

        let explosionCount = initialRolls.filter(die => die === 6).length;
        if (explosionCount > 0) {
            for (let i = 0; i < explosionCount; i++) {
                let extraRoll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1;
                extraRolls.push(extraRoll);
                finalDiceResults.push(extraRoll);
            }
        }

        finalDiceResults.sort((a, b) => b - a);
        let successCount = finalDiceResults.filter(die => die >= successThreshold).length;
        let failureCount = finalDiceResults.length - successCount;
        let countOnes = finalDiceResults.filter(die => die === 1).length;
        let countSixes = finalDiceResults.filter(die => die === 6).length;

        let resultText = `<p><strong>You rolled:</strong> ${initialRolls.join(", ")}</p>`;
        if (explosionCount > 0) {
            resultText += `<p class='italic'>Rolls of 6 explode! Rolling ${explosionCount} extra dice.</p>`;
            resultText += `<p><strong>Extra Rolls:</strong> ${extraRolls.join(", ")}</p>`;
        }
        resultText += `<div class='section-divider'></div>`;
        resultText += `<p><strong>Final Dice Pool:</strong> ${finalDiceResults.join(", ")}</p>`;
        resultText += `<p class='italic'>Successes: ${successCount}, Failures: ${failureCount}</p>`;
        resultText += `<div class='section-divider'></div>`;
        
        let successMessage = successCount >= difficulty ? "ACTION SUCCEEDED!" : "ACTION FAILED!";
        resultText += `<p style='color: ${successCount >= difficulty ? "green" : "red"}; font-weight: bold;'>${successMessage}</p>`;
        
        if (countSixes >= 3 && countOnes >= 3) {
            resultText += `<p style='font-weight: bold;'>Boons and Banes cancelled each other out! The action is a success.</p>`;
        } else if (countSixes >= 3) {
            resultText += `<p style='font-weight: bold;'>Action triggered a BOON!</p>`;
        } else if (countOnes >= 3) {
            resultText += `<p style='font-weight: bold;'>Action triggered a BANE!</p>`;
        }

        output.innerHTML = resultText;
        output.style.display = 'block';
    }
</script>
  3. Save Changes.

✅ Step 3: Refresh & Test

  • Go to your Squarespace page where you added the dice roller.
  • Click "Roll Dice" to test if it's working.
  • If it doesn't work immediately, clear cache (Ctrl+Shift+R) and try again.

🎯 Why Does This Fix It?

  • Squarespace blocks JavaScript inside Code Blocks.
    → Moving the script to Code Injection ensures it runs correctly.
  • Keeps HTML & JavaScript separate, making Squarespace handle the layout properly.

🚀 Let Me Know If It Works!

Try this on your Squarespace site and tell me if the dice roller appears and functions correctly! 🎲🚀

Cheaper Hosting Options for Your HTML Dice Roller

If you want a free or very cheap way to host your HTML file as a simple web page, here are some great options:

✅ 1. GitHub Pages (Free & Easy)

Pros:

  • Free hosting with a simple URL (yourusername.github.io/dice-roller).
  • No coding required after initial setup.
  • Works well if you plan to host more pages (like the card app later).

Steps:

  1. Go to GitHub and create a new repository (pale-tides-dice-roller).
  2. Upload your HTML file (index.html).
  3. Go to "Settings" > "Pages", set branch to main, and save.
  4. Your site is now live at https://yourusername.github.io/pale-tides-dice-roller/.

🔗 Link: GitHub Pages Guide

✅ 2. Netlify Drop (Easiest)

Pros:

  • Drag & drop your HTML file, and it's live instantly.
  • Free URL like pale-tides-dice.netlify.app.
  • No signup needed (but you can create an account to manage the site).

Steps:

  1. Go to Netlify Drop.
  2. Drag & drop your HTML file.
  3. It instantly generates a live URL to share.

🔗 Link: Netlify Drop

✅ 3. Vercel (For Future Expansion)

Pros:

  • Good if you might expand to a full web app later.
  • Custom domain support for free.

Steps:

  1. Sign up at Vercel.
  2. Upload your HTML file as a GitHub repo.
  3. Vercel auto-deploys your site with a free URL.

🔗 Link: Vercel

✅ 4. Neocities (If You Want an Old-School Website)

Pros:

  • Free, and lets you manually edit your HTML in a web-based editor.
  • Works like classic GeoCities.

Steps:

  2. Upload your HTML file.
  3. Site is instantly live!

🔗 Link: Neocities

💡 Best Option for You?

  • Want the easiest solution? 👉 Netlify Drop (no setup, just drag & drop).
  • Want free hosting with a nice URL? 👉 GitHub Pages.
  • Planning a web app later? 👉 Vercel.
